params.body:
Three findings of the same kind: a document that opens without checking whose it is.

**The rental PDF (finding `de-bruikleen-pdf-kan-door-elke-ingelogde`, #579, R S4-9.4).** `RentalController::show` looked the rental up and rendered it. `edit`, `update` and `destroy` all put the dealer of the relation next to the dealer of the signed-in user first; opening did not, and opening is the side that shows the customer's name, address and licence details. It now makes the same comparison, answers 403 when they differ, and 404 for a rental that is not there instead of a 500 on a null.

**The order and the offer (finding `verkeerd-id-geeft-500`, #654, R S1-9.9).** `OrderController::show` and `createFromOffer` threw `Illuminate\Validation\UnauthorizedException`. Laravel does not know that one as an answer, so the dealer got a 500 and the log got an error that was not an error. Both now answer 403 for a foreign dealer and 404 for an id that does not exist.

**The profile photo (same finding).** This turned out to be more than a loud error path. `UserController::image` glued the decoded name behind `storage_path('app/public/')` and returned whatever stood there, so `../../../.env` handed the server's `.env` to any signed-in user. The route is no longer rendered anywhere (its one call in the navigation has been commented out for a long time), but it was still on the router. It now reads through the `public` disk, which cannot leave its own directory, answers 404 for what is not there, and returns nothing that is not an image by its own bytes.

**The platform attachment and the backgrounds (finding `beheerdersinstellingen-zijn-afgeschermd`, #574, R P2-10.1).** Both write paths asked for no right of their own; the shielding hung entirely on the menu right `settings.update`, which every dealer who may save his own settings has. They now ask for the right of the pane they live on, `attachments.index` and `background.index`, the same two rights `getDefaultTab` uses to decide whether a dealer sees those panes at all. The attachment is platform-wide (it is stored with `dealer_id` null), so this is not defence in depth on top of the middleware but the check that was missing.

**Along the way.** `RentalController` read `dealer_id` off `Auth::user()` in six places, which gives the `Authenticatable` contract and not our user model; that stood in the PHPStan baseline as five ignored errors. One typed accessor removes all five. The baseline is six lines shorter and nothing was added to it.

`OfferToOrderTest` pinned the old exception and now pins the 403 plus the absent order. `DocumentsCheckWhoseTheyAreTest` adds seven tests: another dealer's rental and order, an id that does not exist on both, the photo route asked for `../../../.env`, a photo that is not there, and the attachment saved without the right of its pane. All seven were checked against the unfixed code.

Fixes bevinding de-bruikleen-pdf-kan-door-elke-ingelogde, bevinding verkeerd-id-geeft-500, bevinding beheerdersinstellingen-zijn-afgeschermd.
Fixes #579
Fixes #654
Fixes #574

params.title: A document opens only for the dealer it belongs to
